briefing.text: The hypothesis has two parts: KIT mutation enrichment AND focal amplification enrichment in Triple_WT. Check the provided tables (column headers of all files) for any copy-number, CNA, segment or GISTIC field. Focal amplifications need segmented copy-number data; they cannot be inferred from point-mutation calls, and ABSOLUTE ploidy is a whole-genome measure, not a focal amplification. Do not use ploidy or mutation counts as a stand-in. In your reasoning, say which part of the claim the data can test and which it cannot, and choose the label by applying the task's label definitions to that.
briefing.reason: The claim has two parts, and one part may not be testable with these files. Teams need to check this before they let a proxy variable answer that part.

briefing.text: data_clinical_sample.txt already has subtype labels in MUTATION_TYPE (BRAF_Hotspot_Mutants ~150, RAS_Hotspot_Mutants ~92, NF1_Any_Mutants ~28, Triple_WT ~46, NA ~43). Use these labels instead of re-deriving subtypes. Drop NA samples from both groups. Test Triple_WT against all other labelled samples and also against each subtype separately. State which comparison group you used. KIT is reported as roughly mutually exclusive with BRAF/NRAS/NF1.
briefing.reason: If teams re-derive subtypes or keep the NA samples in the comparison group, the enrichment result changes.

briefing.text: data_mutations.txt (274 MB, WGS) contains non-coding and silent variants (Intron, IGR, UTR, Flank, RNA, Silent). When counting KIT mutations, keep only non-silent coding classes: Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Translation_Start_Site, Nonstop. Count each sample at most once per gene. Read the file in chunks with usecols.
briefing.reason: Counting non-coding WGS calls inflates KIT frequencies in every subtype, and with a file this large the analysis needs to be run in chunks.

briefing.text: Melanoma is UV-hypermutated, so many KIT calls are passenger mutations whose rate follows TMB. Driver KIT mutations cluster in hotspots: exon 11 (e.g. V559, L576P), exon 13 (K642E), exon 17 (D816, N822) and exon 9. Report two frequencies per subtype: any non-silent KIT, and KIT hotspot/driver. Compare TMB between subtypes. If TMB differs, also run a logistic regression of KIT status on subtype adjusted for log TMB.
briefing.reason: TMB can confound KIT enrichment differently in different subtypes. Separating driver from passenger KIT calls changes how the result should be read.

briefing.text: The groups are small (Triple_WT ~46) and KIT mutations are rare, so use a two-sided Fisher exact test rather than chi-square. Report counts, percentages, the odds ratio with a CI, and the p-value. Correct for multiple testing (BH or Bonferroni) when you run several subtype comparisons. With small counts, a non-significant result means low power.
briefing.reason: The choice of test and the reading of the result matter when counts are this sparse.

briefing.text: Check denominators. data_gene_panel_matrix.txt marks some samples (~13) as NA, meaning not sequenced for mutations. MAF Tumor_Sample_Barcode may not match the clinical SAMPLE_ID format (e.g. -01 vs -06 suffix), and some patients have more than one sample. A sample with no KIT row counts as wildtype only if it was sequenced. Count the overlap between the MAF and the clinical IDs, and use one sample per patient or report the duplicates.
briefing.reason: ID mismatches and unsequenced samples give wrong mutation frequencies.

briefing.text: data_mutsig.txt holds MutSig significance statistics for the whole cohort, not results by subtype. A significant KIT q-value does not show enrichment in Triple_WT. Base the subtype test on the per-sample MAF joined to MUTATION_TYPE.
briefing.reason: It stops teams from taking cohort-wide significance as evidence of subtype enrichment.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed that support for one half of a two-part conjunctive claim (KIT enrichment), with the other half (focal amplifications) untestable, is enough for the label 'True'. Neither tested this against the task's label definitions. Team A itself names the stricter reading, which gives 'Not verifiable'.

Both treated KIT enrichment in Triple_WT as an empirical finding. Triple_WT is defined by the absence of BRAF/RAS/NF1 mutations, so any driver that is mutually exclusive with those genes is concentrated in it by construction. Neither team asked whether a comparison against a group defined by other drivers is informative here.
Both took MUTATION_TYPE as given and dropped the 43 samples where it is NA, without checking why those samples are unlabelled or whether they carry KIT mutations.
unused_evidence: TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks and Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks in the MAF: both teams set them aside correctly as per-gene annotations. Neither recorded what values they take or showed that they are constant across samples for the same gene, which would confirm they carry no sample-level amplification information.
ABSOLUTE_EXTRACT_PLOIDY in the sample table: rightly not used as a focal-amplification measure. Neither team recorded that they considered it and why it was rejected (Team A only implicitly).

SAMPLE_TYPE / REGIONAL_VS_PRIMARY and the primary-site columns: Triple_WT melanomas may differ in anatomical site or sample type, and neither team checked whether these fields confound the KIT comparison.
Team B used neither TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS nor the Hotspot column, so its KIT count may include UV passenger mutations.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: the focal-amplification half of the claim was reported as untestable, but the label choice ('True' rather than 'Not verifiable') was not resolved. Only the alternative was stated.
Team B: the label rests on 6 KIT-mutant Triple_WT samples, with no hotspot restriction, no TMB adjustment and no multiple-testing note. Its weakest point (focal amps) was reported, not resolved.
second_readings: The claim says Triple_WT is 'characterized by' enrichment of KIT mutations AND focal amplifications. One reading needs both parts supported for 'True'. If one part cannot be tested, the claim as a whole may be 'Not verifiable' rather than 'True'.

'Enrichment' could mean relative to the other subtypes, or relative to a background rate (for example a significant per-gene frequency within Triple_WT). It could also mean driver/hotspot KIT rather than any non-silent KIT call.
challenge.verdict: I trust the KIT part moderately; Team A's hotspot and TMB checks make it fairly solid. I trust the overall 'True' label less, because both teams labelled a two-part claim True after one part proved untestable and neither checked that choice against the task's label definitions.

In hypothesis-evaluation benchmarks that use the labels True / False / Not verifiable, how is a conjunctive hypothesis scored when the data can test one conjunct (and support it) but hold no variable for the other conjunct?
questions.why: Both teams' label depends on whether partial support of a conjunctive claim counts as 'True' or as 'Not verifiable'; neither team showed it knew the convention.

questions.question: In MAFs annotated with Oncotator, what do the TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks and Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks fields contain: a sample-specific copy-number call, or a gene-level annotation taken from a pan-cancer GISTIC peak list?
questions.why: If these fields were sample-specific they would make the focal-amplification part testable; both teams assumed they are gene-level annotations without citing the definition.

findings.question: In MAFs annotated with Oncotator, what do the TCGAscape_Amplification_Peaks and Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks fields contain: a sample-specific copy-number call, or a gene-level annotation taken from a pan-cancer GISTIC peak list?
findings.answer: Gene-level annotation, not a sample-specific call. Oncotator describes its annotations as variant- and gene-centric, drawn from pooled public resources. MAF headers list these sources as fixed, versioned datasets: 'TUMORScape 20100104' and 'TCGAScape 110405'. Tumorscape is the Broad portal of the Beroukhim et al. 2010 (Nature) GISTIC analysis of 3,131 cancers. It reports the most significant amplification and deletion peak regions for each cancer type and the copy-number significance of each gene. TCGA Tumorscape is the same kind of analysis for about 11,000 TCGA cancers. These fields therefore record which published pan-cancer recurrent amplification peaks (by cancer type) contain the mutated gene. They are identical for every sample with a mutation in that gene and say nothing about that tumour's own copy number, so they cannot test sample-level focal amplification. Caveat: none of the pages I read gives a formal column definition; this is inferred from the datasource versions and the portal descriptions.
